input.question: Why are engines measured in 'horsepower'? What does it refer to and how is it calculated?
input.ground_truth: The term Horsepower was first used by James Watt, the man who made great improvements to the steam engine. He used the term to compare the power of his engine to the power of a horse (hence horsepower). Ironically enough, horsepower is a unit of power, while the other commonly used unit of power is the Watt, named after James Watt. So he created a unit that competes with his own name.

Question: Why are engines measured in 'horsepower'? What does it refer to and how is it calculated?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a strong horse that can pull a big cart. A long time ago, people used horses to do a lot of hard work, like pulling wagons and plowing fields.

When cars and engines were invented, people wanted to know how strong these new machines were. So, they decided to compare them to horses because everyone already knew how much work a horse could do.

"Horsepower" is a way to measure how much work an engine can do in a certain amount of time. One "horsepower" is about the same amount of work that one horse can do in one minute, over and over.

So, when someone says a car has 150 horsepower, it means that engine can do the work of 150 horses working together! But don’t worry, there aren’t any real horses inside the car.

How do we calculate it? Well, a long time ago, people made a special rule: one horsepower equals 745.7 watts (which is a measure of power). Or, in old terms, it's about how much work a horse can do lifting 550 pounds up one foot in one second.

But you can just think of it as a way to say, "This engine is as strong as this many horses!"
